newsitem.title: UK: London palladium fixes at lowest in three years.
newsitem.headline: London palladium fixes at lowest in three years.

text.p: Palladium fixed at $116.25 an ounce on Tuesday, the lowest fixing since September 14, 1993.
It had fixed at $116.50 an ounce on Monday afternoon. Prices have been declining steadily since rallying to a high of around $175 an ounce in April 1995.

Dealers said palladium's slide to three-year lows was part of an overall downtrend stemming in recent months from steady supplies from key producer Russia and slack demand from the Japanese electronics industry.
"It's a continuation of that trend, it's being hit from both the supply and demand angles. There hasn't been anything dramatic, it's just drifting off," a dealer said.
Recent attempts to claw above the important $120 an ounce resistance level have met with selling, he added.
Some dealers and analysts saw prices declining still further, first to around $112 an ounce or even below $100.
